gloss: to go, to visit, to make the trip

definitions.gloss: to go, to visit, to take the trouble to come
definitions.explanation: A polite or humble way to express going somewhere, implying effort or deliberate action.

examples.japanese: わざわざ{足|あし}を{運|はこ}んでいただき、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for taking the trouble to come.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{足|あし}を{運|はこ}んで{交渉|こうしょう}した。
examples.english: I visited many times to negotiate.

examples.japanese: ぜひ{店|みせ}に{足|あし}を{運|はこ}んでください。
examples.english: Please do come visit our store.

examples.japanese: {展覧会|てんらんかい}に{足|あし}を{運|はこ}ぶ{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: I plan to visit the exhibition.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {足|あし} (foot/leg) + を + {運|はこ}ぶ (to carry). Literally 'to carry one's feet' to a place.

REGISTER: Polite/formal. Often used in:
- Business contexts
- When thanking someone for visiting
- When inviting customers
- Humble speech about one's own visits

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {行|い}く (to go) - neutral
- いらっしゃる (to come/go) - honorific
- {伺|うかが}う (to visit) - humble
- お{越|こ}しになる (to come) - honorific

COMMON PATTERNS:
- わざわざ{足|あし}を{運|はこ}ぶ (to take the trouble to come)
- {何度|なんど}も{足|あし}を{運|はこ}ぶ (to visit repeatedly)
- ぜひ{足|あし}を{運|はこ}んでください (please do come)
